cards.text: The people have gone back to work on the house of the LORD. Then, on the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD comes through Haggai the prophet. He's to speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, to Joshua, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people.
God gives Haggai a question to ask them, and it starts like this: "Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?"

cards.question: God asks the people how this house looks to them now. Next to its former glory, what does He ask if it seems like?

cards.text: Ouch. That's your buddy scrolling back to your photos from ten years ago and going, "Wow. Look at you back THEN."
But God doesn't leave them sitting in that. He has a word for the governor, for the high priest, and for all the people of the land.

cards.question: God speaks to Zerubbabel, to Joshua the high priest and to all the people of the land. What does He tell each of them?

cards.text: THREE times! Zerubbabel, BE STRONG. Joshua, BE STRONG. Everybody, BE STRONG. Nobody's walking out of this huddle without one.

cards.question: Then God tells them to ___, because He is with them.

cards.text: Then God reaches back into Israel's history. He says this is a promise He already made to them once.

cards.question: God says He made this promise at a big moment in Israel's history. Which moment?

answers.text: When they came out of Egypt

cards.question: God tells the people that His Spirit remains among them, and He tells them not to be afraid.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts looks ahead. He says that once more, in a little while, He's going to shake things.

cards.question: When the LORD of Hosts says He will shake things once more, how much does He say He will shake?

answers.text: Heavens and earth and sea and land
Just the walls of the city

cards.question: God says He will shake all the nations, and they will come with all their armies.
God asked if this house seemed like nothing. Now He says He will fill this house with ___.
Then the LORD of Hosts says the silver is His, and the ___ is His too.

cards.text: Silver? His. Gold? His. Friend, I came home out of a bakery bin for a QUARTER.

cards.question: God says the latter glory of this house will be smaller than the former.
And in this place, God says He will provide ___.

cards.text: From like nothing to a latter glory greater than the former, with peace right in this place. Friend, THAT is how you finish a message.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Even grander than before" is close to what God says in Haggai 2:9 (the latter glory will be greater than the former). A baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Only the right answer starts with "Like" and uses the Bible's own phrase "in comparison." It is also the only answer that fits the awkward question "what does He ask if it seems like?" The right answer stands out from the other two.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move it forward. The joke should ride along on a card that tells the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card restates the answer to card 6 (be strong, three times). It doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The answer is False (armies), but no card ever tells the baker that the nations come with all their treasures (Haggai 2:7). This key detail sets up "The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine" in verse 8, and it is lost.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to complete the wording of the line "The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine." That tests the next words of a line, not its meaning or movement.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke depends on the bakery bin and the 25-cent price, but neither was set up earlier in this lesson. Bakers are only assumed to know about the junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It repeats verse 8, which card 16 already covered, and tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This final card sums up what was already covered (like nothing, then greater glory, then peace) and adds nothing new. It is a recap card.
